topic: Corrected gap-sensitive welfare-budgeted honest-width envelope for the targeting gain in an adaptive contextual experiment. Fix delta in (0,1/4), the Hölder-margin class, a P-independent benchmark policy, and the participant-welfare budget. Define W_{T,delta}(rho) over all non-anticipating designs and all honest interval procedures. Determine the complete frontier up to constants with a procedure-free converse and an attaining adaptive design/interval; optimize fixed-gap and Hölder-local subclasses, retain the compulsory rho^(-1/2) obstruction, and derive rather than assume all other branches, feasibility boundaries, and flattening thresholds. Exact formulas remain answer-open.

open_problems.open_problem: Procedure-free fixed-gap converse: determine the honest targeting-gain interval-width lower envelope over every non-anticipating design satisfying the welfare budget when the fixed benchmark assigns positive mass to an inferior treatment.

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes the Pareto tradeoff between participant regret and treatment-effect estimation error in multi-armed experiments, but not honest width for a nonlinear contextual welfare contrast.
source_refs.author: David Simchi-Levi and Chonghuan Wang

source_refs.claim: All-design first-order efficiency bounds cover assignments using covariates and past outcomes, but do not yield a uniform honest-width frontier under shrinking exploration.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong

source_refs.excerpt: the least-favorable family CONSTRUCTED from primitives (no assumed cube)
The lower bound must be carried by actual bounded-outcome alternatives

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing Pareto results use treatment-effect estimation error, while first-order efficiency bounds do not control every honest interval when exploration can vanish. The first missing step is to turn the participant-welfare restriction into an alternative-dependent sequential information bound and then into coverage-forced separation of the targeting gain. The fixed-gap pair must preserve a P-independent benchmark and change its value contrast; otherwise benchmark cancellation invalidates the claimed compulsory rho^(-1/2) branch. The prior constructions supply offline causal alternatives and adaptive change-of-measure machinery, but neither derives this budget-indexed interval modulus.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A coverage-based lower characterization, uniform over all admissible design-interval pairs, that proves or refutes the rho^(-1/2) fixed-gap obstruction and states its finite-horizon feasibility and flattening thresholds.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its direct conflict between participant welfare and post-experiment scientific precision, replacing estimation error by honest targeting-gain width.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Protect participants through adaptive allocation -> inferior treatments become sparsely observed -> sparse observations limit credible post-experiment inference -> characterize the smallest honest targeting-gain width allowed by a welfare budget

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the bandit change-of-measure inequality and sequential likelihood decomposition, replacing best-arm decision events by events forced by simultaneous interval coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It converts adaptive allocation counts into information bounds without restricting the allocation algorithm, matching the required procedure-free converse.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the ordered testing-modulus reduction from simultaneous coverage to expected confidence-interval length.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is a lower bound for every honest interval, so an estimator-specific variance or regret bound is insufficient.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt predictable weighting of augmented inverse-propensity scores and its variance-stabilized central limit proof for the fixed-gap attaining subproblem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Away from ties, the gain has a regular policy-evaluation component whose precision is controlled by observations of the inferior treatment.

open_problems.open_problem: Scalar-functional local modulus: identify Hölder-margin Gaussian alternatives that genuinely separate the targeting gain under adaptive observation and test the proposed local branches at d=1, beta=1, alpha=1/5 and rho=T^(3/5).

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes pathwise differentiability and inference for optimal treatment value, locating the nonsmooth tie boundary but not its welfare-budgeted minimax width.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.claim: The paper derives minimax rates for nonsmooth L_r functionals in Gaussian white noise, providing machinery for the positive-part component rather than a result under adaptive welfare constraints.
source_refs.author: Yanjun Han, Jiantao Jiao and Rajarshi Mukherjee

source_refs.claim: The paper proves smoothness- and margin-dependent contextual-bandit regret bounds using localized problems; policy-regret separation need not separate the scalar targeting gain.
source_refs.author: Vianney Perchet and Philippe Rigollet

source_refs.excerpt: It gives a lower bound every union-honest interval sequence must obey.
neither the split-sample upper construction nor the two current lower experiments closes the exponent gap

open_problems.why_unsolved: For binary treatment the gain is E[tau_+ - pi0(X)tau], so packed alternatives that change many optimal treatment labels may leave the scalar unchanged; with a balanced benchmark, equal-magnitude sign flips can cancel. The first proof step must therefore build target-separating alternatives or mixtures that satisfy the exact Hölder and margin restrictions before computing their adaptive likelihood distance. The prior honest-value run proves only one sparse-mixture lower component and explicitly leaves an exponent gap, while white-noise functional methods assume a fixed information geometry that must be rederived for endogenous treatment counts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp local modulus or least-favorable-mixture characterization for the targeting-gain functional, including a verified Gaussian early-kill construction that explicitly validates or falsifies the presolve feasibility and oracle-width exponents.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its distinction between learning an optimal treatment rule and conducting inference on the rule's population value.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Personalized treatment improves population welfare -> the optimal value is nonsmooth at treatment ties -> classification-hard alternatives can cancel for the scalar gain -> determine the correct local honest-information modulus

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt polynomial approximation, bias control, and least-favorable-prior arguments for nonsmooth scalar functionals, replacing fixed white-noise information by adaptive arm-specific information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The positive-part target contains an integrated absolute-value functional, so classification-error lower bounds can miss its estimation difficulty.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine target-separating local alternatives with the adaptive change-of-measure inequality and a coverage-to-testing reduction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The information available within each bump depends on earlier observations and treatment assignments.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse smooth localized alternatives and margin bookkeeping, but redo separation for the scalar gain rather than cumulative policy mistakes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its hard-instance geometry matches the Hölder-margin model and isolates the first calculation that must change.

open_problems.open_problem: Uniform budget-saturating exploration: can a predictable allocation learn the cheap-to-explore Hölder-margin regions, obey the participant-welfare budget, and supply the information needed by a targeting-gain interval throughout the feasible budget range?

source_refs.claim: The paper balances stratum-specific randomized-trial lengths for a CATE error-regret frontier, but its contextual model has finite features and fixed-order nonzero gaps.
source_refs.author: Jiachun Li, Kaining Shi and David Simchi-Levi

source_refs.claim: The paper attains smoothness-dependent minimax regret using nonparametric regression and selective exploration, without honest uncertainty under a prescribed welfare budget.
source_refs.author: Yichun Hu, Nathan Kallus and Xiaojie Mao

source_refs.claim: Weighted augmented inverse-propensity policy learning attains minimax regret conditional on a diminishing-exploration regime rather than choosing exploration subject to a welfare budget.
source_refs.author: Ruohan Zhan, Zhimei Ren, Susan Athey and Zhengyuan Zhou

source_refs.excerpt: No matched feasible minimax rate is asserted in the strict-gap branch
whether weak-arm nuisance learning imposes the slower conditional exponent

open_problems.why_unsolved: Finite-stratum balancing can use observed stratum arrivals and fixed gaps, whereas here the informative regions and their welfare prices are unknown, small-gap regions may be rare, and early elimination can destroy the benchmark-arm observations needed for inference. The first changed step is a uniform predictable-count argument that controls local information and gap-weighted welfare cost simultaneously from the design's own data. The prior proposal obtains only a conditional clipped-AIPW upper bound under supplied weak-arm nuisance rates; regret-optimal allocation and inference under an assumed exploration floor do not prove the required self-generated guarantee.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A primitive-level uniform exploration lemma and implementable allocation rule giving simultaneous high-probability bounds on welfare expenditure and local effective information, or a counterexample locating the infeasible budget regimes and saturation thresholds.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its explicit budget-to-estimation-accuracy formulation while making continuous covariates and scalar targeting gain the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Heterogeneous participants require treatment-specific evidence -> collecting that evidence spends participant welfare -> finite-stratum balancing no longer applies to unknown smooth gap regions -> learn a budget-feasible information allocation

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the ConSE construction that learns arrival frequencies and balances later randomized-trial lengths, together with its count and estimator analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It jointly accounts for welfare loss and inferential information; learned continuous cells and vanishing gaps are the new components.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt local-polynomial reward estimation and selective exploration over shrinking uncertainty regions, adding a proof of budget saturation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the smooth-context learning mechanism needed before exploration can be priced by unknown treatment gaps.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt augmented inverse-propensity estimation, truncation, and martingale inference while rechecking their conditions under budget-driven assignment probabilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The allocation guarantee must feed a valid causal interval rather than stop at regret or sample-count control.

open_problems.open_problem: Attaining honest interval: can a connected two-sided interval uniformly control the targeting-gain optimization remainder and adaptive score variance under budget-driven vanishing exploration, matching the converse across fixed-gap and Hölder-local laws?

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs uniformly valid lower confidence bands for optimal welfare and shows that margin separation governs regularity, but it is one-sided and not welfare-budgeted.
source_refs.author: Kirill Ponomarev and Vira Semenova

source_refs.claim: CADR obtains asymptotic normality for a fixed contextual policy value through conditional-variance stabilization, not a uniform interval for a learned optimum.
source_refs.author: Aurélien Bibaut, Maria Dimakopoulou, Nathan Kallus, Antoine Chambaz and Mark van der Laan

source_refs.claim: The paper provides nonasymptotic off-policy confidence sequences under adaptive logging, but the target policy is evaluable and the optimality remainder is absent.
source_refs.author: Ian Waudby-Smith, Lili Wu, Aaditya Ramdas, Nikos Karampatziakis and Paul Mineiro

source_refs.excerpt: converts an expected local-polynomial policy-regret bound into coverage by Markov calibration
constructing a connected interval attaining n^{-ξ} up to logarithms over the same ordered pair
predictable-QV lower growth alone does not

open_problems.why_unsolved: Adaptive policy-evaluation intervals cover a fixed policy value; substituting a learned optimizer adds a nonsmooth optimality remainder that is of first order near ties and cannot be omitted. Pointwise variance stabilization also does not imply uniform coverage along Hölder-margin sequences whose welfare budget drives propensities toward zero. The first missing step is a uniform decomposition into an evaluable predictable contrast, an explicitly bounded optimization bias, and a studentized martingale remainder with design-verifiable information growth. The prior honest-value interval uses conservative Markov calibration and leaves the matching connected interval open, while the quadratic-variation run assumes rather than derives the crucial dynamics-to-pivot bridge.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully specified adaptive estimator and connected interval with uniform 1-delta coverage and a matching expected-width upper bound, or a sequential counterexample stating where optimization bias or studentization prevents attainment.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its optimal-welfare inference arc and explicit role for treatment-margin separation, then identify two-sided budgeted adaptive width as the new endpoint.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Policy optimization defines a welfare target -> near ties make plug-in optimal-value inference nonregular -> adaptive welfare budgets create vanishing information -> construct a connected honest interval that controls both optimization bias and score variance

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt conditional-variance estimation and CADR stabilization, proving uniform remainder and variance bounds at the proposed frontier scales.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It handles contextual adaptive dependence, while the learned optimum supplies the additional nonsmooth remainder.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt bias-aware honest interval calibration, deriving its bias envelope from Hölder smoothness, margin mass, and realized exploration rather than assuming negligible nuisance error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unresolved upper bound is an honest-width problem with binding nonparametric bias, not merely variance estimation.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt online optimal-value estimation and its treatment-rule remainder analysis, rederiving the remainder when randomization probabilities shrink with the welfare budget.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the optimized causal value itself rather than a fixed off-policy value.

literature_map:
Simchi-Levi and Wang (2023, AISTATS), Multi-armed Bandit Experimental Design, occupy the noncontextual treatment-effect error-regret Pareto tradeoff.
Li, Shi and Simchi-Levi (2024, ICML), Privacy Preserving Adaptive Experiment Design, extend that tradeoff to finite feature sets and fixed-order gaps.
Perchet and Rigollet (2013, Annals of Statistics), The Multi-Armed Bandit Problem with Covariates, supply smoothness-margin regret geometry.
Hu, Kallus and Mao (2022, Operations Research), Smooth Contextual Bandits, provide nonparametric selective exploration under Hölder smoothness.
Gur, Momeni and Wager (2022, Operations Research), Smoothness-Adaptive Contextual Bandits, show the extra cost of unknown smoothness; smoothness adaptation is outside this fixed-class run.
Luedtke and van der Laan (2016, Annals of Statistics) locate optimal-value nonregularity at treatment ties and supply an inference donor.
Han, Jiao and Mukherjee (2020, PTRF) show that nonsmooth scalar-functional estimation needs machinery distinct from policy classification.
Hadad et al. (2021, PNAS) and Bibaut et al. (2021, NeurIPS) provide adaptive weighting and conditional-variance stabilization for policy evaluation.
Waudby-Smith et al. (2024, ACM/IMS JDS) and Cook, Mishler and Ramdas (2024, CLeaR) provide nonasymptotic coverage and efficient adaptive-estimation tools.
Howard et al. (2021, Annals of Statistics) supply time-uniform martingale boundaries, whose logarithmic overhead need not be intrinsic at fixed T.
Zhan, Ren, Athey and Zhou (2024, Management Science) prove policy-learning regret under a supplied diminishing-exploration regime rather than a chosen welfare budget.
Ponomarev and Semenova (2024, revised 2025) construct one-sided optimal-welfare bands and show the role of margin separation.
Firpo, Galvao and Parker (2023, Journal of Econometrics) explain the directional differentiability issue created by marginal optimization.
Kaufmann, Cappé and Garivier (2016, JMLR) give an allocation-agnostic sequential change-of-measure donor; the exact all-design honest-width envelope and the presolve branches were not located in this bounded scan.
prior_proposal_map:
The active stat_welfare_budgeted_width_frontier/v2 directory contained no earlier proposal core, rejected angle, or reviewer JSON, and no upgrade parent was supplied.
The closest banked runs were stat_policy_regret_margin_overlap/v1, stat_optimal_value_honest_adaptation/finite_action_margin_tie_union, stat_neyman_regret_minimax/v1, and exp_bandit_random_qv_studentization_frontier/v1.
The accepted policy-regret core's honest_scope and oeq:feasible-tight leave a conditional weak-arm-learning upper bound unmatched in the strict-gap branch.
The optimal-value README, current and angle-0-rejected cores, proposal_angle0_rejected.tex, and reviews/angle1_v3.json were inspected; the rejected TeX was a placeholder, while the JSON contained the substantive abandoned construction.
The optimal-value reviewer strengthening_paths[2] asks for a connected interval matching the lower scale, and the README says the exact union-honest expected-length frontier remains open.
The Neyman-regret core and angle0_v2 review supply a bounded adaptive-likelihood construction for a different loss, so they are method evidence rather than a duplicate result.
The bandit-QV README, core, and angle0_v10 review isolate the unproved dynamics-to-uniform-pivot bridge and demand an explicit uniform error bound.
The accepted discrete-optimal-value core was also checked; it excludes uniform confidence intervals and vanishing overlap, so its scalar-risk result does not close this adaptive-width problem.
All prior-proposal transfers were combined with independent web evidence before G1-G5 filtering.
